title: Understanding Drainage Slope Principles
description: Achieving the correct slope in horizontal gravity drainage piping is essential for maintaining a self-scouring velocity. A common misconception is that a steeper slope is always better. In reality, if a drain line has insufficient pitch, wastewater flows too slowly, allowing heavy solids to settle along the pipe invert and build up obstructions. Conversely, an overly steep slope allows liquids to rush ahead, leaving solid waste behind to dry and clog the pipe. Always follow local code requirements and verify continuous pitch with a spirit level to ensure smooth, efficient waste removal across the entire system.

Understanding Drainage Slope Principles

Achieving the correct slope in horizontal gravity drainage piping is essential for maintaining a self-scouring velocity. A common misconception is that a steeper slope is always better. In reality, if a drain line has insufficient pitch, wastewater flows too slowly, allowing heavy solids to settle along the pipe invert and build up obstructions. Conversely, an overly steep slope allows liquids to rush ahead, leaving solid waste behind to dry and clog the pipe. Always follow local code requirements and verify continuous pitch with a spirit level to ensure smooth, efficient waste removal across the entire system.
